findings.fact: Bidders must submit 2 copies of their bid in sealed envelopes or packages labeled with the item description and department, including company name and address, to the City Clerk by the deadline.

findings.title: Out-of-State Corporation Registration
findings.fact: Out-of-state corporations must qualify or register to transact business in Rhode Island in accordance with the Rhode Island Business Corporation Act.

findings.title: MBE/WBE Participation Goal
findings.fact: The City has a 20% MBE/WBE combined participation goal. If not met, a Waiver Request Form must be submitted.
findings.business_implication: Meeting the 20% MBE/WBE goal may be a factor in award evaluation. If not met, a waiver must be submitted and approved; otherwise, the bid may be considered non-responsive.

findings.title: Apprentice Requirements
findings.fact: For construction projects valued at $100,000 or more, bidders must comply with the City's ordinance requiring not less than 15% of total hours worked by apprentices.
findings.business_implication: The project likely exceeds $100,000, so the bidder must commit to using apprentices for at least 15% of total labor hours. Non-compliance may affect payment and contract performance.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan to meet the apprentice requirement by partnering with apprenticeship programs or hiring apprentices. Ensure compliance reporting processes are in place for payment requisitions.

quotes.quote: Attention of prospective bidders is called to the fact that this project is to be bid upon and executed under the City of Providence Code of Ordinances Chapter 21 Art. findings.title: First Source Requirements
findings.fact: The project is subject to the City's First Source Ordinance requiring hiring Providence residents. Compliance reporting is a condition for payment.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must commit to hiring Providence residents and maintain detailed records to demonstrate compliance. Failure to meet these requirements could delay or prevent payment.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the First Source Ordinance requirements, prepare a hiring plan to meet the resident hiring goals, and establish a system for tracking and reporting compliance with each payment requisition.

findings.fact: The project requires licensed and qualified environmental and demolition contractors. The selected contractor must be a RI licensed asbestos abatement contractor.

findings.action_recommendation: Verify that the firm holds all necessary Rhode Island licenses, including the asbestos abatement contractor license, and include proof of licensure in the bid submission.

findings.fact: Bidders must not submit sensitive information (like tax ID, insurance, good standing) in the initial bid; it will be requested after award. Submitting such information early may lead to disqualification.

findings.title: Sensitive Information Submitted Directly to Department May Be Disqualifying
findings.fact: Bidders who submit sensitive information directly to the issuing department in an attempt to protect pricing terms from becoming public will be disqualified.

findings.fact: The City of Providence is exempt from Federal Excise Taxes and Rhode Island Sales Tax, so prices quoted are not to include these taxes.

findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that all quoted prices exclude Federal Excise Taxes and Rhode Island Sales Tax. Verify that your pricing structure aligns with this requirement before submission.

findings.title: Assignment Prohibition
findings.fact: The contractor will NOT be permitted to assign or underlet the contract, or assign any monies without prior written consent of the City Purchasing Director.

findings.action_recommendation: Review the contract to ensure all intended subcontractors and financing arrangements are acceptable, and seek written consent from the City Purchasing Director if any assignment is contemplated.

quotes.quote: The contractor will NOT be permitted to: a) assign or underlet the contract, or b) assign either legally or equitably any monies or any claim thereto without the previous written consent of the City Purchasing Director.

findings.title: Prevailing Wage Rates
findings.fact: State law provisions concerning payment of prevailing wage rates apply for many contracts involving construction, alteration and/or repair work.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must pay workers at least the prevailing wage rates set by state law, which may increase labor costs and require compliance with reporting and record-keeping requirements.
findings.action_recommendation: Determine if the contract falls under the prevailing wage law, and if so, budget for higher labor costs and ensure compliance with wage and hour regulations.

quotes.quote: For many contracts involving construction, alteration and/or repair work, State law provisions concerning payment of prevailing wage rates apply (RIGL Sec. 37-13-1 et seq.)

findings.title: No Work Without Purchase Order

findings.action_recommendation: Ensure a purchase order is received and verified before commencing any work or delivery, and maintain documentation of the purchase order for billing purposes.

quotes.quote: No goods should be delivered, or work started without a Purchase Order.

findings.business_implication: The bidder must provide the required financial assurance (e.g., certified check, bid bond, or performance bond) as specified in the bid documents, or its bid will be rejected. This may involve significant upfront costs and potential liability.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully review the bid documents to determine which financial assurance is required, and prepare the necessary funds or bonds to accompany the bid. If a performance bond is required, ensure the bidder can obtain one.

findings.title: Award Timeframe and Firm Prices

quotes.quote: Awards will be made within nighty (90) days of bid opening. All bid prices will be considered firm, unless qualified otherwise. Requests for price increases will not be honored.

findings.title: No Limitation of Liability
findings.fact: The City does not agree to limit the contractor's liability to the price of the Agreement or any other monetary limit.

findings.action_recommendation: Assess the potential liability exposure and consider whether additional insurance coverage or risk mitigation strategies are needed. Consult legal counsel to understand the full implications and explore options to negotiate a limitation of liability clause.

quotes.quote: The City shall not subject itself to any contractual limitations on liability. The City shall have the time permitted within the applicable statute of limitations, and no less, to bring or assert any and all causes of action, suits, claims or demands the City may have arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the work provided in the Agreement, and in no event does the City agree to limit your liability to the price of the Agreement or any other monetary limit.

findings.fact: The Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Rhode Island, and all actions must occur in Rhode Island state or federal court.
findings.business_implication: The bidder will be subject to Rhode Island law and must litigate any disputes in Rhode Island courts, which may be inconvenient and costly if the bidder is located elsewhere.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the cost and practicality of litigating in Rhode Island. Consider consulting with local counsel and factor potential travel and legal expenses into the bid.

quotes.quote: The Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Rhode Island. You expressly submit yourself to and agree that any and all actions arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the Agreement or relationship between the parties shall occur solely in the venue and jurisdiction of the State of Rhode Island or the federal court located in Rhode Island.

findings.title: No Dispute Resolution or Binding Arbitration
findings.fact: The City is not required to submit to dispute resolution or mandatory/binding arbitration.
findings.business_implication: The bidder has limited options for resolving disputes; the City cannot be forced into arbitration, so the bidder may have to resort to litigation in Rhode Island courts, which could be time-consuming and expensive.
findings.action_recommendation: Be prepared for potential litigation in Rhode Island. Consider including dispute resolution mechanisms in the bid or negotiating for a more balanced approach, though the City may not agree.

quotes.quote: With regard to any issues, claims, or controversies that may arise under this Agreement, the City shall not be required to submit to dispute resolution or mandatory/binding arbitration.

findings.title: Indemnification Obligation
findings.fact: The contractor must indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the City from all claims and damages arising from the work.
findings.business_implication: The bidder assumes significant liability for any claims or damages related to the work, including legal fees, which could be substantial and impact profitability.
findings.action_recommendation: Review insurance coverage to ensure it adequately covers indemnification obligations. Consider negotiating to limit indemnification to the extent caused by the City's negligence, though the City may not accept.

quotes.quote: To the fullest extent permitted by law, you shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the City, its employees, officers, agents, and assigns from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, allegations, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, obligations, fines, penalties, judgments, liabilities, costs and expenses, including but not limited to attorneys’ fees, of any nature whatsoever arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the work provided in the Agreement.

findings.title: Insurance Requirements
findings.fact: The contractor must maintain insurance coverage required by the RFP or commercially reasonable coverage, and name the City as an additional insured on general liability and umbrella policies.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must secure and maintain appropriate insurance, which adds to project costs. Naming the City as an additional insured may increase premiums and administrative burden.
findings.action_recommendation: Obtain insurance quotes early and factor costs into the bid. Ensure compliance with additional insured requirements and provide certificates of insurance as required.

quotes.quote: You shall maintain throughout the term of this Agreement the insurance coverage that is required by the RFP or, if none is required in the RFP, insurance coverage that is considered in your industry to be commercially reasonable, and you agree to name the City as an additional insured on your general liability policy and on any umbrella policy you carry.

findings.title: Apprentice Requirements
findings.fact: The project must utilize not less than 15% of total hours worked by apprentices, and compliance reporting is a condition for payment.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must allocate a portion of work hours to apprentices, which may affect labor costs and scheduling. Failure to meet the requirement or submit reports could delay payment.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan to meet the apprentice hour requirement by partnering with apprenticeship programs or hiring qualified apprentices. Establish a system for tracking and reporting hours to ensure compliance and timely payment.

quotes.quote: This ordinance outlines requirements for utilizing not less than 15% of total hours worked by apprentices.

Compliance reporting shall be submitted with any contract payment requisition, in a format to be specified by the City. This demonstration of compliance through such reports shall be a condition of the requisition for payment to be processed.

findings.title: Bid Submission Requirements
findings.fact: Complete responses must be received by Monday, July 27, 2026, at 2:15 pm and sent to the City Clerk. No faxed or electronic submissions will be accepted.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure physical delivery of the complete bid to the specified location by the exact deadline. Late or electronic submissions will be rejected, risking disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for physical delivery well in advance, using a reliable courier or hand delivery, and confirm receipt with the City Clerk's office. Verify the address and allow extra time for potential delays.

quotes.quote: Complete responses must be received by Monday, July 27, 2026, at 2:15 pm and sent to the City Clerk (25 Dorrance Street Providence, RI 02903 Room 311). No faxed or electronic submissions will be accepted.

findings.title: MBE/WBE Participation Requirements
findings.fact: Minority business enterprises must be awarded a minimum of 15% of the dollar value of the entire procurement or project, with 7.5% to minority-owned and 7.5% to women-owned businesses.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must allocate at least 15% of the contract value to certified MBE/WBE firms, with specific sub-targets for minority-owned and women-owned businesses. Failure to meet these requirements could lead to non-compliance and potential loss of award.
findings.action_recommendation: Identify and engage certified MBE/WBE subcontractors or suppliers early, ensuring they meet the required percentages. Document all participation commitments and be prepared to report within 10 days of Notice of Award.

quotes.quote: Under Rhode Island General Laws §37-14.1, Minority business enterprises shall be included in all procurements and construction projects under this chapter and shall be awarded a minimum of fifteen percent (15%) of the dollar value of the entire procurement or project. Of that fifteen percent (15%), minority business enterprises owned and controlled by a minority owner, shall be awarded a minimum of seven and one-half percent (7.5%), and minority business enterprises owned and controlled by a woman shall be awarded a minimum of seven and one-half percent (7.5%).

findings.title: Prevailing Wage Requirements
findings.fact: Any construction over $1,000 is required by state law to pay state prevailing wage, and certified payrolls must be submitted.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must pay prevailing wages for all construction work exceeding $1,000 and submit certified payrolls for all contractors and subcontractors. Non-compliance can result in payment delays or legal penalties.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the applicable prevailing wage rates from the Rhode Island Department of Labor and Training, incorporate these costs into the bid, and establish a system to collect and submit certified payrolls promptly to avoid payment delays.

quotes.quote: Prevailing Wages: Any construction over $ 1,000.00 is required by state law to pay state prevailing wage. A current copy of the most recent Prevailing Wage scale is obtained from the State of Rhode Island, Department of Labor and Training, Division of Professional Regulation or at the Davis-Bacon Wage Determination link. It is also by request for each construction bid document. All vendors supplying construction services must submit certified payrolls from any contractor and sub-contractor who work on the project. No payments are made until all payrolls are up to date, and correct.

findings.title: No Interest on Overdue Payments
findings.fact: The City is not obligated to pay interest on overdue invoices, and contractor cannot recover collection costs.
findings.business_implication: The bidder will not receive interest on late payments and cannot recover collection costs, increasing financial risk if the City delays payment. This may impact cash flow and profitability.
findings.action_recommendation: Factor potential payment delays into financial planning, maintain sufficient cash reserves, and consider negotiating shorter payment terms or milestone payments in the contract. Ensure all invoices are complete and accurate to avoid processing delays.

quotes.quote: In no circumstances shall the City be obligated to pay or shall you be entitled to receive interest on any overdue invoice or payment. In no circumstances shall the City be obligated to pay any costs associated with your collection of an outstanding invoice.

findings.title: No Dispute Resolution or Binding Arbitration
findings.fact: The City is not required to submit to dispute resolution or binding arbitration; disputes may only be resolved in court.
findings.business_implication: The bidder cannot compel the City to enter arbitration or mediation, and disputes must be resolved in court, which can be costly and time-consuming. This limits alternative dispute resolution options.
findings.action_recommendation: Be prepared for potential litigation by documenting all communications and contract performance. Consider including dispute resolution clauses in subcontracts, and seek legal advice on dispute management strategies.

quotes.quote: With regard to any issues, claims, or controversies that may arise under this Agreement, the City shall not be required to submit to dispute resolution or mandatory/binding arbitration. Nothing prevents the parties from mutually agreeing to settle any disputes using mediation or non-binding arbitration.

findings.title: Bid Bond Liquidated Damages
findings.fact: If a bid bond is required, the amount may be retained as liquidated damages in case of default.
findings.business_implication: If the bidder fails to sign and deliver the contract after winning, the bid bond amount will be forfeited as liquidated damages, representing a direct financial loss.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that the bid is accurate and that the bidder has the capacity and intention to enter into the contract if awarded. Review the bid bond amount and consider the risk of forfeiture before submitting.

quotes.quote: A bid bond in the amount of           per centum (%) of the proposed total price, must be deposited with the City Clerk as a guarantee that the contract will be signed and delivered by the bidder; and the amount of such bid bond shall be retained for the use of the City as liquidated damages in case of default.

findings.title: Performance and Payment Bond Requirement
findings.fact: If required, contractor must post a performance and payment bond equal to 100% of the contract amount.
findings.business_implication: The contractor will need to secure a bond for the full contract value, which may involve additional costs and affect cash flow. Failure to obtain the bond could lead to disqualification or default.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for the bonding requirement early. Obtain quotes from surety companies and ensure the bid price accounts for bonding costs. Verify that the company can secure the bond before bidding.

quotes.quote: A performance and payment bond with a satisfactory surety company will be posted by the bidder in a sum equal to one hundred per centum (100%) of the awarded contract.

findings.title: No Assignment Without Consent
findings.fact: Contractor cannot assign the contract without prior written consent; unauthorized assignment is voidable.
findings.business_implication: The contractor cannot transfer its rights and obligations under the contract to another party without the City's consent. This limits flexibility in subcontracting or selling the business.
findings.action_recommendation: If the contractor anticipates needing to assign the contract, seek the City's written consent in advance. Ensure all subcontracting arrangements comply with this clause.

quotes.quote: You shall not assign your rights and obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the City. Any assignment without prior written consent of the City shall be voidable at the election of the City.

findings.title: No Waiver of Rights
findings.fact: City's failure to enforce any provision does not waive its right to enforce later.
findings.business_implication: The City can enforce any term at any time, even if it has previously overlooked a breach. This means the contractor cannot rely on past leniency as a defense.
findings.action_recommendation: Maintain strict compliance with all contract terms throughout the contract period. Do not assume that the City's inaction on a breach waives its right to enforce later.

quotes.quote: The failure of the City to require performance of any provision shall not affect the City’s right to require performance at any time thereafter, nor shall a waiver of any breach or default of this Agreement constitute a waiver of any subsequent breach or default or a waiver of the provision itself.

findings.title: Default for Failure to Deliver or Meet Specifications
findings.fact: Failure to deliver within the time quoted or failure to meet specifications may result in default in accordance with the general specifications.
findings.business_implication: If the contractor fails to deliver on time or does not meet the specifications, it may be declared in default, leading to termination, financial penalties, and potential damage to reputation.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that the bid includes realistic delivery timelines and that the contractor has the capability to meet all specifications. Monitor progress closely and communicate proactively with the City if issues arise.

quotes.quote: Failure to deliver within the time quoted or failure to meet specifications may result in default in accordance with the general specifications.

findings.title: Conflicting Information on MBE/WBE Forms Requirement
findings.fact: The Bid Package Checklist states MBE/WBE forms must be completed for EVERY bid, but the Supplemental Information section says certain items are not requested in the initial bid. This is not a direct contradiction but could be ambiguous.
findings.business_implication: Bidders may be uncertain whether MBE/WBE forms are required at the initial bid submission or only after award, potentially leading to incomplete submissions or unnecessary paperwork.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify with the purchasing department whether MBE/WBE forms are mandatory for the initial bid or only upon request after award. Ensure all required forms are included to avoid disqualification.

quotes.quote: *Please note: MBE/WBE forms must be completed for EVERY bid submitted and must be inclusive of ALL required signatures. Forms without all required signatures will be considered incomplete.
This information is NOT requested to be provided in your initial bid that you will submit to the City Clerk’s office by the “date to be opened” noted on page 1.
